name: update-at-relocated-storage-target
description: An `update` of an element the model stores under a file name that is not its identity. The store finds an element by what it declares, never by a path recomputed from its name, so the update is written into the file that declares the element and nowhere else — no second file is created and no other element's file is touched. `create-at-occupied-storage-target` is the same store seen from the verb that allocates a file; this is the verb that finds one: a file whose name is not its element's leaves the element editable through the protocol.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model plus one hand-authored file, `data_types/implementation/Speed_kph.yaml`, whose declared name is `VehicleSpeed_kph`. The element is addressable by its identity — `read {implementation_types, VehicleSpeed_kph}` answers — and the file it lives in is named otherwise. The commit rewrites `data_types/implementation/Speed_kph.yaml` and creates no `data_types/implementation/VehicleSpeed_kph.yaml`.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the requested address exactly, and an address never names a file — so where the element is stored is not something an approval could have covered or refused.

input.intent: Record vehicle speed in metres per second.

expected.notes: `committed`, and not a safety act. The file is located by content through one identity-to-file index per layer, built once per change set, so a change set touching fifty elements of one layer parses that layer once. The one refusal left on this verb is an element NO file of its layer declares, which a snapshot read from the same tree cannot produce from a well-formed request; it stays `consistency-violation` at the element. No storage path appears in the response, and the file name the element happens to live under is neither reported nor changed — renaming it is a user's act outside the protocol, and changes no generated artifact.
